rounds.text: Aurum Proptech Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum, evidenced by a 73% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 138% compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E19]. This aggressive operational scaling is backed by a rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100, which carries a high confidence BUY rating supported by strong YoY sales and net profit growth [E61, E64]. Profitability is structurally improving at the core, with operating margins expanding significantly to 25% in the trailing twelve months compared to just 1% three years prior [E28]. Furthermore, the company is generating substantial liquidity, reporting positive operating cash flow of Rs 63 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 47 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34], all while maintaining a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.22x and slightly reducing borrowings year-over-year [E35, E37]. Valuation metrics also look attractive relative to sector benchmarks, with a price-to-book ratio of 1.54x against a sector benchmark of 1.96x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.71x compared to the sector benchmark of 10.84x [E7, E11]. Conceded: [E13] that return on equity stands at -3.8% and promoter holding has decreased to 38.09% as of September 2026 [E39].

The valuation for Aurum Proptech Ltd is heavily bloated, illustrated by an eye-watering P/E ratio of 131x alongside a dividend yield of 0.00% [E1, E4]. Profit quality is further called into question by the explicit warning that recent earnings include a massive other income component of Rs 91.1 Cr [E60], masking the true core operating performance of the business. Beneath the headline growth figures, historical profitability metrics are deeply distressed, featuring a 10-year compounded sales growth of -7% and a 10-year compounded share price growth of -4% [E14, E20]. Return metrics underscore this chronic underperformance, with a 10-year median ROE of -1%, a 5-year median ROE of -12%, and a recent ROE of -3.8% [E24, E25, E13]. Furthermore, structural insider commitment is waning, demonstrated by promoters slashing their holding from 50.34% in Dec 2023 down to 38.09% in Sep 2026, alongside a flagged low interest coverage ratio and decelerating earnings growth [E39, E57, E66]. conceded: E15, E16, E17, E19, E42, E43

The bear’s fixation on the 131x P/E ratio ignores the far more relevant P/B of 1.51x and the favorable sector comparisons where the P/E sits at a modest 22.48x and EV/EBITDA at 7.71x against higher sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7, E11]. The concern regarding historical struggles is firmly eclipsed by a powerful modern inflection, demonstrated by massive 5-year sales growth of 109%, 3-year sales growth of 44%, and a soaring 73% expansion over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16, E17]. Furthermore, profit growth has exploded by 138% in the TTM while operating margins surged by 24 percentage points over three years to reach 25%, proving the core engine is fundamentally accelerating [E19, E28]. Operational strength translates directly into hard cash, with the company generating substantial operating cash flow of Rs 63 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 47 Cr in March 2026, backed by conservatively managed debt-to-equity of 0.22x [E33, E34, E35]. Valuation is fully supported by independent DCF modeling pointing to an intrinsic value of Rs 291 per share, leaving a healthy margin of safety of 26.9%, which is reinforced by an elite rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 [E42, E43, E61]. conceded: E39, E60

The bull dismisses the 131x P/E ratio by pointing to a P/B of 1.51x and alternative valuation metrics, but this ignores the fact that high P/E multiples directly highlight severe earnings compression and an expensive entry price [E1, E2, E68]. While the bull celebrates surging short-term sales and profit growth, it glosses over the fundamental reality that 10-year compounded sales growth sits at a negative -7% and 10-year share price growth is -4% [E14, E20]. The claim of a robust operational core is heavily undermined by a low return on equity of -1.15% to -12.4% over various recent periods, a median 10-year ROE of -1%, a meager 3.23% ROCE, and explicitly flagged low interest coverage [E9, E10, E24, E57, E59]. Furthermore, the bull's narrative of pure operational acceleration is complicated by the disclosure that earnings include Rs 91.1 Cr of other income, masking the true operational contribution [E60]. Conceded: E15, E19, E33, E34, E42.
